sections.title: Intake
sections.conclusion: Baseline fields and source anchors establish whether the proposal can be reviewed at all.

sections.title: Claims and evidence
findings: Proposal document read by reasoning layer: yes
Requested: Treasury withdrawal to reimburse the lost Ikigai Info governance action deposit and claimed lost staking rewards.
Recipient: Ikigai Info governance action submitter / intended recipient; specific identity or address not stated in document

Deliverables: Reimburse the claimed 100,000 ADA lost governance action deposit, Pay an additional 3,000 ADA for claimed lost staking rewards, Distribute funds directly on-chain to the intended recipient upon enactment
Deadline/expiry: Instantly as part of governance action enactment on-chain
Claim (governance, independently_verifiable, medium materiality): An Info governance action titled Cardanoの生きがい - Ikigai - was submitted in September 2024 shortly after the Chang hard fork.

Claim (governance, proposer_asserted, low materiality): The Ikigai Info governance action was symbolic and asked the community to agree with a statement thanking contributors and expressing hope for Cardano's future.

Claim (technical, proposer_asserted, high materiality): A Cardano node bug permitted an unregistered stake key to be used in the governance action, preventing the submitter from recovering the 100,000 ADA deposit.
Claim (governance, proposer_asserted, medium materiality): The proposer says there was significant community sentiment that the submitter should be reimbursed for the lost deposit.
Claim (governance, proposer_asserted, medium materiality): The Cardano in Oceania initiative included this reimbursement in its budget Info governance action, but that action was not approved.

Claim (economic, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): The requested 103,000 ADA consists of the original 100,000 ADA deposit plus 3,000 ADA for claimed lost staking rewards calculated at 2% per annum.
missing: Independent evidence for: A Cardano node bug permitted an unregistered stake key to be used in the governance action, preventing the submitter from recovering the 100,000 ADA deposit.
Independent evidence for: The proposer says there was significant community sentiment that the submitter should be reimbursed for the lost deposit.
Independent evidence for: The Cardano in Oceania initiative included this reimbursement in its budget Info governance action, but that action was not approved.
Independent evidence for: The recipient has not previously received funds from the Cardano treasury.
sections.conclusion: Each claim must map to replayable public evidence; proposer assertions alone are not enough for confidence.

sections.title: Treasury analysis
findings: Six-month treasury flow regime: unsustainable (basis: total inflow (tau + donations) vs enacted withdrawals)
sections.conclusion: Treasury votes require a higher bar because they consume shared ADA and create precedent.

sections.title: Risk review
sections.conclusion: Risk is not a side note; unmitigated execution or governance risk can dominate an otherwise attractive proposal.

sections.title: Counterargument pass
findings: Strongest YES: the proposal substantiates "An Info governance action titled Cardanoの生きがい - Ikigai - was submitted in September 2024 shortly after the Chang hard fork." and clears the evidence gates.

Strongest NO: a material claim is unsupported — "A Cardano node bug permitted an unregistered stake key to be used in the governance action, preventing the submitter from recovering the 100,000 ADA deposit." — so cost or precedent may outweigh the benefit.
Strongest hold: if claims cannot be tied to replayable evidence, abstaining avoids overclaiming certainty.
sections.conclusion: A defensible rationale must show the best opposing case before it reaches a vote.

sections.title: Synthesis
findings: Final vote must be derived from completed sections above, not from a prose summary.
The public rationale should name the decisive section and the strongest counterargument.
sections.conclusion: The vote is only credible if the assessment tree shows enough work for a skeptical delegator to audit.
